mainTopic: The two names in בת היענה, signs of kosher and non-kosher birds, and the signs and named species of kosher חגבים
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof. A סופר writes בת היענה as two words, so it is two names, and the egg is forbidden too. The גמרא challenges this from כדרלעמר and answers that only בת היענה may be split even across two lines. Next, a ברייתא on the משנה's rule about a bird that is דורס gives several signs of non-kosher and kosher birds. Some signs come from the bird's body, some from how it grips a cord, some from how it catches food, and one from the birds it lives with. אביי narrows the air-catching sign to a bird that also eats in the air. The גמרא also shows that the rule of אחרים can fit the רבנן, since it requires living with the other birds and also looking like them. The גמרא then turns to חגבים. רב פפא requires that the wings cover most of the length and most of the circumference, and a ברייתא permits a חגב that will grow its signs later. The amud ends with two teachings that identify the kosher locust species in the פסוק and add more species from the words 'למינו'. The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two separate words means two names
steps.stepSummary: The scribe writes בת היענה as two separate words, which shows they are two names.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the scribe splits it into two words, we learn that they are two names.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof that בת היענה is really two names, because a סופר writes it as two separate words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בת is its own word, it can mean 'daughter of the יענה', which is the egg. So the egg is included in the prohibition. The proof rests on how the name is written in a ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Words
Conclude from this; we learn from it
Names
A non-kosher bird listed in the תורה; literally 'daughter of the יענה'

phrases.english: into two words,
phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier sentence: the scribe splits בת היענה (ויקרא 11:16) into two words.

phrases.english: conclude from it that they are two names.

steps.raayaObject: That בת היענה is two names, so the egg is also forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: The scribal practice of writing בת and היענה as two separate words

steps.title: Challenge from the name כדרלעמר
steps.stepSummary: כדרלעמר is also written as two words, yet it is one person's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, what about כדרלעמר, which the scribe splits into two? Would you say that it is also two names?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof: splitting a name into two words does not have to mean it is two names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כדרלעמר is clearly one king's name, yet it is written as two words. So writing a name as two words cannot prove two names, and the proof about בת היענה seems to fall.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so; if that logic were right (opens a challenge)
The scribe who writes a ספר תורה
Splits, divides

phrases.english: But if that is so,
"Chedorlaomer"
which the scribe splits in two,
is it also so that they are two names?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that two written words means two names
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample: כדרלעמר is written as two words but is one name

steps.title: Split across lines versus split into words
steps.stepSummary: כדרלעמר may not be split across two lines, but בת היענה may be, so it is truly two names.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: There, he splits it into two words, but he does not split it across two lines. But here, he splits it even across two lines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a stronger kind of split that only בת היענה gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both names are written as two words. But only בת היענה may have its two words on two different lines. That shows a full separation, so the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Lines of writing
There / here (contrasting two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: בת היענה is two names, because it may be split even across two lines. This is unlike כדרלעמר, which is one name. So the egg is included.

phrases.english: They say:
There, he splits it into two words,
but into two lines he does not split it,
but here,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁנֵי שִׁיטִין נָמֵי פָּסֵיק לְהוּ.
phrases.english: he splits it even into two lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם בִּשְׁתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת פָּסֵיק לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from כדרלעמר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any split into two words would mean two names, so כדרלעמר would be two names
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a split allowed even across two lines shows two names, and that applies to בת היענה

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about any bird that claws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words: the חכמים said any bird that is דורס is non-kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: But the חכמים said: Any bird...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives one general sign for a non-kosher bird: it claws its prey. The next steps bring a ברייתא with more signs.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages
Bird
Claws its prey, holding it down with its feet to eat it

phrases.english: But the Sages said:
Any bird.
phrases.notes: Only the opening words are quoted; the משנה goes on to say that any bird that is דורס is not kosher.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any bird that is דורס is non-kosher

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's signs of kosher and non-kosher birds
steps.stepSummary: A bird that claws and eats is surely non-kosher. A bird with an extra toe, a crop, and a gizzard that peels is surely kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבן גמליאל says: A bird that claws its prey and eats it is surely non-kosher. A bird that has an extra toe, a crop, and a gizzard that can be peeled is surely kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings רבן גמליאל, who gives one sign of a non-kosher bird and three signs of a kosher bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clawing proves a bird is non-kosher. Having all three kosher signs together proves a bird is kosher. The word בידוע means these are certain signs.

keyTerms.meaning: It is known for sure
An extra toe, set higher at the back of the foot
Crop, the pouch in the throat where food collects
A gizzard whose inner lining peels off
Non-kosher / kosher

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabban Gamliel says:
One that claws and eats is surely non-kosher;
if it has an extra toe and a crop
and its gizzard can be peeled, it is surely kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A ברייתא that expands on the משנה's sign
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clawing and eating means non-kosher; an extra toe, a crop, and a peelable gizzard mean kosher

steps.title: The string test of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: Have the bird stand on a stretched string. If it splits its toes two and two, it is non-kosher. If it splits them three and one, it is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: We stretch a string for the bird. If it splits its toes, two on this side and two on that side, it is non-kosher. If three are on this side and one on that side, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא gives a practical test: how the bird grips a string with its toes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds that grip with two toes on each side are non-kosher. A bird that holds three toes in front and one behind is the kosher type.

keyTerms.meaning: We stretch
A cord or rope
Splits its toes

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
We stretch a cord for it,
phrases.notes: The bird is made to stand on the cord, and we watch how it grips.

phrases.english: if it splits its feet,
two on this side and two on that side, it is non-kosher;
three on this side and one on that side, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר: מוֹתְחִין לוֹ חוּט שֶׁל מְשִׁיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another opinion in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A two-and-two grip means non-kosher; a three-and-one grip means kosher

steps.title: A bird that catches food in the air
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says any bird that catches food out of the air is non-kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Any bird that catches food out of the air is non-kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The third opinion in the ברייתא gives another sign of a non-kosher bird: catching food in the air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sign is about how the bird hunts, not about its body. The next step will test this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Catches, snatches
Air

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עוֹף הַקּוֹלֵט מִן הָאֲוִיר – טָמֵא.
phrases.english: Any bird that catches food from the air is non-kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עוֹף הַקּוֹלֵט מִן הָאֲוִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last opinion in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird that catches food from the air is non-kosher

steps.title: Challenge from the ציפרתא
steps.stepSummary: The ציפרתא also catches food in the air, yet it is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ציפרתא also catches food in the air!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: there is a kosher bird that also catches food in the air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If catching in the air makes a bird non-kosher, the ציפרתא should be non-kosher. But it is known to be kosher, so the rule seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of small kosher bird
It surely catches (food in the air)

phrases.english: But the tziparta also catches food in the air!
phrases.notes: The challenge assumes the ציפרתא is a kosher bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's sign
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that any bird that catches in the air is non-kosher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample: the kosher ציפרתא also catches in the air

steps.title: Only a bird that catches and eats in the air
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the rule is about a bird that both catches and eats in the air.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They mean a bird that catches and eats in the air.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by making the rule narrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The non-kosher sign is a bird that eats its food while still in the air. The ציפרתא catches food in the air, but it lands before eating it, so it stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Catches and eats (in the air)
They are saying; this is what they meant

steps.whatToRemember: Catching food in the air is a non-kosher sign only when the bird also eats it in the air.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They are saying "catches and eats."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ציפרתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any catching in the air makes a bird non-kosher
steps.terutzMaskana: Only catching and eating in the air does; the ציפרתא lands before it eats

steps.title: Others say: a bird is judged by the birds it lives with
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say that a bird living among non-kosher birds is non-kosher, and a bird living among kosher birds is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: If a bird lives with non-kosher birds, it is non-kosher. If it lives with kosher birds, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with one more sign, given by אחרים: you can tell a bird's status by the company it keeps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-9 used the bird's body and behavior: its toes, its crop, and how it eats. אחרים add a social sign. Where the bird lives and who it lives with tells us whether it is טמא or טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name for a תנא whose view is quoted without his name
Lives with, dwells among
Non-kosher / kosher (here, for birds)

phrases.english: Others say:
If it dwells with non-kosher birds, it is non-kosher;
if with kosher birds, it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a last sign to the ברייתא's list of bird signs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird that lives among טמאים is טמא, and a bird that lives among טהורים is טהור.

steps.title: Whose view is this? Perhaps רבי אליעזר's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion אחרים follow and suggests רבי אליעזר, who said the זרזיר lives with the crow because it is the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It seems to be רבי אליעזר's. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says that the זרזיר did not go to live next to the crow for no reason. It went there because it is the same kind of bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know which known opinion אחרים match. It suggests רבי אליעזר, who also judged a bird by the bird it lives with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says the זרזיר stays with the crow, a non-kosher bird, because it belongs to the crow's kind. That would make the זרזיר non-kosher, which looks just like the rule of אחרים. If this is right, אחרים would follow only רבי אליעזר and not the רבנן, who argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like whom?' The גמרא is asking which תנא's view this follows
Not for nothing; there is a reason behind it
A kind of bird (often said to be a starling) that lives near crows
Crow, raven (a non-kosher bird)
Its kind or species

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
Like Rabbi Eliezer, as it is taught:
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְחִנָּם הָלַךְ זַרְזִיר אֵצֶל עוֹרֵב,
phrases.english: Not for nothing did the zarzir go to the crow,
but because it is of its kind.
phrases.notes: Since it is the crow's kind, it would be non-kosher just like the crow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose opinion the statement in step 10 follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא agrees with אחרים that a bird is judged by the birds it lives with
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggested answer: רבי אליעזר, because of his teaching about the זרזיר and the crow

steps.title: It can fit the רבנן too: the bird must live with them and also look like them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that אחרים follow only רבי אליעזר. The rule speaks about a bird that both lives with the other birds and looks like them.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows the רבנן. We are talking about a bird that lives with them and also looks like them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 11 and shows that אחרים can match the רבנן as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living together alone is not enough. The bird must live with the other birds and also look like them. The זרזיר lives with the crow but does not look like it, so the רבנן can still call it kosher and agree with אחרים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can even say.' The גמרא shows the rule can fit another view too
Looks like, resembles
The majority of חכמים, who argue with רבי אליעזר

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule of אחרים is 'live together, so you are the same.' Here the גמרא reads it as needing two things: living together and also looking alike.

phrases.english: You may even say it is the Rabbis;
we are speaking of one that dwells with them and resembles them.
phrases.notes: The זרזיר lives with the crow but does not look like it, so the רבנן can still say it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 11 by narrowing what the rule of step 10 means
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that אחרים must follow רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed that living together is enough. The rule actually needs living together and also looking alike.

steps.title: For חגבים: what counts as 'most of its body'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's signs of a kosher חגב and asks what 'most of it' means when the wings must cover most of its body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And with חגבים, any that has...' and so on. What does 'most of it' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: the משנה's signs for kosher חגבים. It asks what 'the wings cover most of its body' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of the signs in the משנה is that the wings cover most of the body. A body can be measured more than one way, so 'most' is unclear. The גמרא wants a precise measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Grasshoppers and locusts; some kinds are kosher
'And so on.' The quote from the משנה continues
Most of it (here, most of its body)

phrases.english: And with regard to grasshoppers, any that has etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: four legs, four wings, two jumping legs, and wings that cover most of its body.

phrases.english: What is 'most of it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, moving from birds to חגבים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to measure the 'most of its body' that the wings must cover

steps.title: Two versions of רב: most of the length, or most of the circumference
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב that it means most of its length. Another version says רב meant most of its circumference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: most of its length. Some say he said: most of its circumference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רב's teaching, but it was handed down in two different versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one version, the wings must reach along most of the body's length. In the other, they must wrap around most of its girth. We are not sure which version is correct, and the next step settles this.

keyTerms.meaning: Its length
Its circumference, how far around the body

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Most of its length;
and some say: most of its circumference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Most of its length, or in another version, most of its circumference

steps.title: רב פפא: the wings must cover both
steps.stepSummary: Since we are unsure which version is right, רב פפא rules that the wings must cover most of the length and also most of the circumference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, we need most of its length, and we also need most of its circumference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the doubt from step 14 by requiring both measurements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know which version of רב is correct. So to be safe, a חגב is kosher only if its wings meet both conditions. If it is missing either one, it is not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
We require

steps.whatToRemember: A kosher חגב's wings must cover most of its length and also most of its circumference (רב פפא).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore,
we require most of its length,
and we require most of its circumference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the two versions of step 14 by requiring both
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The wings must cover both most of the length and most of the circumference.

steps.title: A חגב that will grow its signs later is permitted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a חגב which does not have its signs now but will grow them later, like the זחל, is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If it does not have them now but will grow them later, like the זחל, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a new rule: a young חגב that has not grown its signs yet is still kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We look at what the creature will become, not only at what it has today. If its signs are going to grow in, it already counts as kosher now.

keyTerms.meaning: Now
Will grow (them) in the future
A young חגב that has not yet grown its signs
Permitted

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If it does not have them now
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the kosher signs from the משנה.

phrases.english: but will grow them after a time,
such as the zachal, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related rule about the signs of חגבים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חגב that will grow its signs later is permitted even now.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי learns it from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי reads 'אשר לא כרעים' to teach that a חגב without jointed legs now, which will grow them later, is still kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי says: 'Which have no jointed legs' teaches that even though it does not have them now, and will grow them later, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי gives a source in the תורה for the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the word 'לא' is written with an א, meaning 'not', even though it is read as 'לו', meaning 'has'. So the פסוק hints that a חגב which does not yet have jointed legs, but will grow them, is still included among the kosher ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Jointed legs (the jumping legs of a חגב)
Even though

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, says:
"Which have [lo] jointed legs":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:21. It is written לא ('not') but read לו ('has'), so it hints at one that does not have them yet.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו
phrases.english: even though it does not have them now
and will grow them after a time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from a פסוק for the rule of step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'אשר לא כרעים' includes a חגב that will grow its jointed legs later.

steps.title: What is a זחל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what creature the ברייתא means by 'זחל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a זחל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of an unfamiliar word that the ברייתא used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 gave the זחל as its example but did not say what it is. The גמרא wants to identify it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is?

phrases.english: What is a zachal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word used in step 16

steps.title: אביי: it is the אסקרא
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the זחל is the creature called אסקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is the אסקרא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with the Aramaic name of the creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי gives the everyday name people used, so the learner can recognize which creature the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: The Aramaic name for the זחל

phrases.english: Abaye said: Askera.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18

steps.title: The four kosher locusts named in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק listing the kosher locusts and gives the everyday name of each of the four species.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'These of them you may eat: the ארבה...' The ארבה is the גובאי, the סלעם is the רשון, the חרגול is the ניפול, and the חגב is the נדיאן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that names, in the language people actually used, each of the four locust species the תורה permits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses names like ארבה and סלעם, but people did not always know which bug each word meant. The ברייתא matches each תורה name to a familiar local name, so you know exactly which creatures are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The first kosher locust species named in the פסוק
The second kosher locust species named in the פסוק
The third kosher locust species named in the פסוק

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'after its kind' four times?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what we learn from the word 'למינו / למינהו' appearing four times in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the פסוק say 'after its kind', 'after its kinds', 'after its kinds', 'after its kinds', four times?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא notices that the פסוק adds 'after its kind' after each of the four species and asks what these extra words are for. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have just listed the four species. Since every word in the תורה must teach something, the four extra words 'למינו' must be adding something.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why does the פסוק need to say this?' Asks what extra words come to teach

steps.title: Four more kosher species are included
steps.stepSummary: Each 'למינו' adds another kosher species: the ציפורת כרמים, the יוחנא ירושלמית, the ערצוביא and the רזבנית.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include the ציפורת כרמים, the יוחנא ירושלמית, the ערצוביא and the רזבנית.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the four 'after its kind' phrases add four more species that are also kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One extra 'למינו' for each species means one extra species for each. So the kosher locusts are not only the four named in the פסוק, but eight in total.

steps.confusionAlert: Even though it is called a 'bird' (ציפורת), the ציפורת כרמים is a type of locust, not a real bird.

steps.whatToRemember: The four 'after its kind' phrases add four more kosher locusts, so there are eight in total.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק as general and specific
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל explains the same פסוק through the method of כלל ופרט: each 'למינו' is a general term and each named species is a detail, starting with ארבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: These are the general terms, and these are the details. 'ארבה' is the גובאי; 'after its kind' comes to include...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching, from the school of רבי ישמעאל, that reaches the extra species through his rule of כלל ופרט וכלל. The amud ends in the middle of this teaching, and it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, each 'למינו' simply added a species. Here the 'למינו' phrases are treated as general terms around the specific named species. By רבי ישמעאל's rules, a general term after a detail adds things similar to that detail. So it starts with ארבה (the גובאי), and 'למינו' will add something like it.

keyTerms.meaning: The general terms, here the 'למינו' phrases

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the same extra species can be derived by two different methods of reading the פסוק.
